prerequisites: It is advisable to have the knowledge of Physics and Mathematics taught in high school.

learning_outcomes.text: To study the basic concepts and laws of Classical Mechanics, Fluid Mechanics, Oscillatory and Wave Motion, and Thermodynamics in the field of Engineering.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is typically at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences typically demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and problem-solving within their field of study.
Understanding and interpretation of texts and data, development of skills for their concretization and clear and concise exposition.
Aptitude for the distribution of resources and time and their implementation in real situations.
Ability to transmit concepts, ideas, processes, etc., related to Industrial Engineering orally and in writing, clearly and correctly.
Ability to use scientific-technical tools for solving calculation and design problems in Industrial Engineering and aptitude for seeking sustainable engineering solutions.
Ability for teamwork and ability to develop multidisciplinary projects.
Ability to relate to other people and open aptitude towards the creation of new relationships.
Ability to incorporate new knowledge in the area of Industrial Engineering, based on the acquired training and necessary for the evolution of technology.
Development of autonomy and creativity capabilities, enhancing aptitudes for the development of own initiatives and undertaking new projects.
Understanding and mastery of basic concepts about the general laws of mechanics, thermodynamics, fields, waves and electromagnetism and their application to solving problems typical of engineering.
